title: Storms Disrupt Thanksgiving Travel and Delay the Macy's Parade
summary:
Thanksgiving travel hit a stormy snag this year — and so did one of America's most famous parades. Powerful storms swept across the United States on Thursday, November 26, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, snow in parts of the Midwest, and flooding along the California coast. About 81.5 million people were expected to travel for the holiday between Thursday and Monday, according to AAA, and hundreds of flights had already been cancelled or delayed by early Thursday morning. On the West Coast, unusually high tides called king tides flooded streets and knocked off part of Pacifica Pier, prompting evacuation warnings. On the East Coast, meteorologist Richard Bann of the National Weather Service warned of wind, heavy rain, and coastal flooding from a storm with many dangers at once. The East Coast storm was expected to mostly clear out by Saturday, easing weekend travel home.

The weather also changed Thanksgiving parade plans. In New York City, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Wednesday that the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade would be postponed to Saturday, November 28. It would have been the parade's 100th, with a record 100 giant balloons. The parade was cancelled before during World War II, but this is the first time in its 100-year history that it will take place on a day other than Thanksgiving. Organizers said it took two years to prepare the celebration, with over 11,000 participants and volunteers, thousands of high school marching band musicians, and hundreds of balloon handlers. Mamdani said safety was the top priority, warning of sustained winds of 30 to 40 miles per hour, gusts as high as 65 miles per hour, and possible floods. Philadelphia also grounded all balloons for its parade this year because of the winds.
why_it_matters: Storms can change holiday plans for millions of families, so knowing the forecast helps people travel safely and stay ready when big events move.

background_read: Thanksgiving is a big holiday in the United States when many families travel to spend time together, so travel is very busy around that day.
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is a famous parade in New York City with giant balloons, marching bands, and thousands of people taking part.
Strong winds can be dangerous for giant balloons, because they can blow them off course, so parade leaders may move the parade or keep the balloons on the ground to keep people safe.
Very high tides, called king tides, happen when the moon and sun line up to pull the ocean higher than usual, which can flood streets near the coast.
